_what: Everything the files core knows about the files contract and the folder it shows, as DATA (src/data.rs reads it once). The core names no operation, field, status, word or number in code: each is here. `call` is how one contract operation travels: an HTTP request of `method` to the computer's origin plus `path` with {operation} filled, its input as the JSON body (a name never travels in a URL: f1 bug 20). `operations` maps each job of the core to the contract operation that does it (tools/live-namespace/src/account_files/account-files-routes.json `operations`); one the contract does not offer yet is null, and the core refuses that job as `not_offered` instead of doing it another way. `fields` are the names of the fields the core reads from a contract answer and writes into a request. `problems` map an answer to the one OS-neutral problem set every shell maps to its own (src/errors.rs): the first row whose `status` matches (and `failure_code`, when the row names one) wins; an answer the rows do not name is `unreachable`, so the core asks the next computer (a 503, or a 409 `namespace_origin_not_bound` from a copy that may not write the real store). The statuses are the contract's own (account-files-routes.json `folder.statuses`); a 404 with no code is an operation the computer does not serve. The folder a core shows (its root id, name and contract folder) is the shell's setup, read from the computer's row, so one computer may show several folders, one core each. `identity` is the content identity form (BLAKE3, the contract's `1f:` multihash prefix, tools/live-namespace/src/account_files/write.rs). `upload_id_hex_chars` is the contract's upload id length (write.rs validate_upload_id). `bounds` names where each number the core plans with comes from in the contract's own settings (tools/live-namespace/src/account_files/settings.json): the host reads them and hands them in at setup, and tests/numbers.rs holds these names to that file. `absent_version` is the `expected_version` that says a name must not exist yet (account-files-routes.json `_folder`). Pins are the contract's own pin rule rows naming items (`pin_*` fields; the contract answers `kept` per name for the device that asks); ignore rules are the person's rule rows the core decides itself. `trash_id` is the OS's trash container, which lists nothing (deleted names go to the contract's set-aside tree, Recently Deleted). `item_facts` are the facts of one item an ignore rule may name, with the field kind that picks its comparisons (tools/formula-engine/rules/rule-operators.json `applies_to`); `item_kinds` are the contract's row kinds, which the facts' `kind` reads as well. `conflict_name` writes the plain name a conflicting edit is kept under, beside the other version: {stem}, {device}, {date} and {ext}; `conflict_name_again` the same when that name is taken too, with {n} counting from `conflict_first_again`.
